title: Meter anomaly dashboards + alerts (billing deltas, spend spikes, missing dimensions)
author: Allison Grant
release_notes:
- Adds Grafana dashboards for meter deltas + anomaly indicators
- Adds alert rules that page #eng-sre and notify #finance with runbook links
- Adds backfill suppression + invoice-run awareness to reduce false positives
body:
Context
We’re seeing recurring “invoice vs console vs telemetry” confusion during the metering sanity checks program. Finance needs earlier signal on anomalies (before invoices are generated), and SRE needs actionable alerts that link directly to the triage flow.

This PR adds a small set of opinionated dashboards + alerts focused on usage/billing meters:
- Meter delta monitoring (raw telemetry aggregates vs billing-ready aggregates)
- Spend spike detection (per account / per model family)
- Missing-dimension and schema regressions (e.g., null region/model, unexpected model alias)
- Negative / impossible counters (e.g., negative cached tokens, output_tokens > total_tokens)

Dashboards
1) Billing Meter Health — Overview
- Global status tiles (last 24h): reconciled vs unreconciled, max delta %, #accounts over threshold
- Top offenders table (account_id, workspace_name, meter_name, delta_pct, delta_units)
- Facet filters: env, region, model_family, endpoint_type, customer_tier

2) Meter Delta Drilldown
- Delta distribution histogram + p95/p99 over time
- Timeseries of delta_units and delta_pct (by meter_name)
- Correlates deltas with request_outcome and retry_reason when present (best-effort; dims may be missing until ENG-4823 lands everywhere)

3) Usage Spend Anomalies
- Per-account spend estimate (billing-ready) with z-score + day-over-day thresholds
- Split by endpoint_type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
- “Newly-active account” indicator to avoid paging on first-time usage ramps

4) Meter Schema/Dimension Quality
- % null / unknown for model, region, endpoint_type
- Cardinality guardrails (model_alias explosion, unexpected retry_reason values)
- “dimension drift” panel that flags new enum values not seen in last N days

Alerting
Alerts are routed as follows:
- #finance: non-paging notifications with a short summary, dashboard link, and runbook link
- #eng-sre: paging alerts only for high-confidence issues (schema regressions, large deltas sustained > 30m, global missing dimensions)

New alert rules
- meter_reconciliation_delta_pct_high
  - Triggers if delta_pct > 0.75% for any of the critical meters (input_tokens, output_tokens, embedding_units) AND delta_units > 50k over 1h (to avoid noise on small accounts)
  - Severity: warn to #finance; page #eng-sre only if > 2% and sustained 30m

- meter_dimension_missing_global
  - Triggers if > 0.1% of events in last 15m are missing region or model_id in prod
  - Severity: page #eng-sre

- meter_spend_spike_account
  - Triggers if account spend estimate is > 3.5 stddev above trailing 14d baseline AND absolute increase > $250
  - Severity: notify #finance only (no page), since many spikes are legitimate launches; the goal is pre-invoice review

Backfill suppression / false positive controls
- Adds a “backfill_window” label + alert inhibition rule to suppress delta/spike alerts during known backfills.
- Adds an optional invoice_run_id filter so dashboards can show “latest run” vs “all time windows”, reducing churn when Finance re-runs invoice aggregation.

Runbook links
- Finance triage: Confluence → Finance & Legal / RevRec & Billing / Billing discrepancy triage runbook
- Eng triage: Internal SRE runbook section “Meter anomalies (billing deltas)” + pointers to the reconciliation job output

Testing / validation
- Validated dashboard JSON renders in Grafana staging.
- Fired synthetic alerts in staging using replayed meter data with injected null dimensions.
- Verified Slack routing in #finance-test and #eng-sre-test.

Notes / follow-ups
- These alerts assume the daily reconciliation job exists and is producing the comparison series (ENG-4821). If the series is missing, the dashboards still render but will show a “no data” banner.
- Once ENG-4823 lands broadly, we should tighten the drilldown panels to segment billed vs non-billed outcomes explicitly.

Screenshots
- Added to the PR comments (Grafana staging URLs + render snapshots).

review_conversation:
Emily Stone (Billing controls): Can we make sure the #finance notification includes the acceptance threshold language? Finance is using 0.5% as a soft threshold but we said 0.75% here.
Allison Grant (author): Good catch. I aligned the alert to 0.75% to reduce noise, but I’ll add the message text to explicitly call out: “Finance review threshold 0.5% (soft), SRE threshold 0.75%/2% (hard)”. Pushed in 2d0c8a1.

Logan Wright (Telemetry/analytics): The delta series name should match what ENG-4821 is emitting: meter_delta_pct (not reconciliation_delta_pct). Otherwise the panels will be empty.
Allison Grant: Updated queries + legend labels to match meter_delta_pct / meter_delta_units. Also added a “series missing” annotation panel to make it obvious when the job hasn’t run.

Nadia Rahman (Metering pipelines): Please add an inhibition for backfills; we trigger re-aggregation weekly and it’s going to light up #finance.
Allison Grant: Added inhibit rule keyed on backfill_window=true and documented how to set it during backfills. Also added a note to post in #finance when inhibitions are enabled.

Cole Summers (Billing hooks): For spend spike alerts, can we exclude accounts on free credits to avoid noise from “effective $” swings?
Allison Grant: We don’t have a reliable “credit_applied” dimension in the observability pipeline yet. I added a minimum absolute increase ($250) and a “newly_active_account” dampener. Follow-up item: add credit flag once it’s in the export schema.

Rishi Malhotra (FP&A): The spend estimate should be clearly labeled as “billing-ready usage * list price”, not invoice total.
Allison Grant: Renamed panels to “Estimated usage charges (list)” and updated the dashboard description.

Final approvals
- Emily Stone: Approved
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Nadia Rahman: Approved
- Cole Summers: Approved
